annotations.text: The de inesse (material) reading of Peirce's married-woman proposition: ∃w∃h — a married woman with a husband — and a scroll 'if he fails, she suicides'. Two generic lines of identity cross into the scroll: pure Beta. Peirce's complaint (CP 4.546): this is true if the husband simply never fails — the conditional asserts no connection. What he reached for with the tinctures — 'it is NOT POSSIBLE that he fails without her suiciding' (the blue-tinted figure of Ms 490) — needs worlds, and lives next door in 'would_be_courses' as a branching DAG of courses of experience.
